HariMultiThread Ultimate 2.4.9 - Vulkan Hybrid
Verified release: all 13 broad native client profiles, three focused original C2ME 9.8 profiles, and dedicated/production gates passed on these exact JAR bytes.

Minecraft 1.20.1 / Forge 47.4.23 / Java 17

Installation
Use one copy of this Hari JAR in the Forge profile's mods directory. Replace the previous HariMultiThread/Async JAR. The Forge Vulkan renderer is included; remove a separate VulkanMod JAR. Retain the normal dependencies of each additional mod.

C2ME Forge is optional. The reproducible test inputs are stock 0.2.0-forge.9.6 (CurseForge file 8929972) and stock 0.2.0-forge.9.8 (file 9040801). All third-party input JARs are unchanged. The broader 13-profile matrix uses 9.6; 9.8 has focused OptiFine, Distant Horizons and Aether+Midnight checks. The final test index records each accepted original profile and complete artifact hash.

Rendering
Compatible profiles use the merged Vulkan renderer. External renderers and shader integrations select the complete OpenGL route before Vulkan renderer initialization; Hari async processing and its separate Vulkan collision backend remain available. Fabulous graphics also retain the OpenGL renderer. This preserves the original rendering features in the tested profiles.

The external GL contract recognizes 111 exact overloads. Untranslated external compute/shader calls and 2,248 unsupported overloads select OpenGL rather than pretending to implement a Vulkan equivalent.

Included repairs and performance work
- Pair original C2ME LIGHT addition/removal levels after Mixin merge. Identify actual release operations across Forge and OptiFine names, retain original owner queues, removal and exceptions.
- Restore original duplicate-entity-tracking exceptions, preserve intentional entity/client fault propagation and saved-world reopen.
- Preserve Rubidium cleanup/acquire/invalidate ownership, original provider chunk scheduling, native mob AI and saved NBT.
- Retain pooled chunk work, batched region uploads, correct draw/upload/draw dependencies, Vulkan lifetime and swapchain repairs, strict shader resources and zero-loss collision fallback.

Performance evidence
The current equivalent-work Java queue/upload benchmark processes 5,120,000 work items per sample. The recorded median changes from 60.42 ms to 14.17 ms; allocation changes from 123,360,000 to 21,120,000 bytes. 128 disjoint regions use one copy command with both required graphics/transfer dependencies. These component measurements are separate from Minecraft hardware FPS.

Commands
/async stats - inspect async work
/async gpu - inspect the device/collision path
/async gpu test - compare actual GPU collision candidates with the CPU reference
/async gpu toggle - change and persist the operator GPU-collision setting

Verification scope
The native tests use installed forgeclient Minecraft, dedicated servers and Linux Mesa software Vulkan/OpenGL. They include original Aether portals and Midnight rifts, all spawn-egg mob types with original AI, original whirlwind expiry, chunk unload/return, chest NBT, resource reload, actual resizing and clean same-world reopen in a distinct JVM. The shader profile retains MakeUp-UltraFast 9.5f. The automated Vulkan test environment uses the checksum-pinned official Khronos SDK 1.4.363.0 for the final Midnight/combined-dimension profiles, with full core and synchronization validation and the actual loaded library hash verified. Slow software tests temporarily use 480 × 270 only to operate original double-Space controls, then restore 1280 × 720 for every scene and 300-frame sample; no flight timer, game state, shader option or original physics is overridden.

This proof covers the recorded profiles and paths. Windows/macOS hardware, hardware FPS, every boss combat phase and arbitrary packs remain outside this native proof. Rubidium's upstream Lucent dynamic-lighting limitation is not represented as repaired by a no-crash test.
